edges.description: Pointed at immune and inflammatory activation rather than at vascular resistance, because that is where the cited sentences actually land: one names a high-salt environment among the contributors to immune activation in this disease, which is this node's own content. The second item is carried because it limits the first, recording that the mechanistic contribution of salt to blood-pressure sensitivity is not clearly understood, so the route beyond this node stays open. Only those two are carried. The salt-sensitivity prevalence figure sizes the susceptible population rather than arguing for this edge, so it stays on the exposure, where it already was.

Graded below the sodium link into this same node, and the difference is in the sentences rather than in the biology. The salt link has a sentence naming salt as a contributor to immune activation; this one has a sentence saying only that these mechanisms link the disease with obesity among several other conditions, which asserts co-membership without a direction or a route. Recorded as modulating rather than predisposing for exactly that reason: the field would support predisposing, but nothing carried here states a direction, and the predicate should not assert what the evidence beneath it does not.

nodes.description: Angiotensin receptor blockers occupy AGTR1, withdrawing the AT1-mediated vasoconstrictor and aldosterone drive that the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone node above supplies and that raises vascular resistance. Recorded as its own node because this entry's ARB treatment acts at the receptor rather than on the dysregulation itself, while the ACE inhibitor treatment acts upstream, on angiotensin II generation, and points at the dysregulation node instead. The node carries no causal edge on purpose: its relation to the mechanisms above is inhibitory, and a downstream edge would assert that receptor blockade causes them. The treatments that act here name it in their target_mechanisms instead.

nodes.description: The molecular target of beta-blocker therapy in hypertension, and the receptor through which `Sympathetic Nervous System Overactivity` acts on both the heart and the juxtaglomerular apparatus. Blockade lowers blood pressure by two routes the entry already models separately: reduced cardiac output, and reduced renin release feeding `Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System Dysregulation`. The node exists so that the beta-blocker entry in `treatments`, which previously named no mechanism at all, points at the receptor rather than at nothing. The node carries no causal edge on purpose, because its relation to the driver it suppresses is inhibitory while a `downstream` edge asserts causation, so there is no honest edge to draw from a blockade node to the mechanism it blunts. It is a treatment anchor, reached through the treatment's `target_mechanisms`, the same shape the merged mu-opioid conformers use.

nodes.description: Chronic immune activation involving both innate and adaptive immunity drives vascular inflammation and remodeling. T cells, monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells infiltrate target organs including arteries, kidneys, heart, and brain, releasing proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-17, IFN-gamma, and TNF-alpha that elevate blood pressure and cause end-organ damage.
